exercise.name: Back Forward Leg Swings

reference.title: Back Forward Leg Swings (male)
reference.listing: GymVisual page could not be read (gymvisual.com blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching knowledge

exercise.mechanics: Dynamic hip flexion and extension on one leg
exercise.laterality: Unilateral (swing the other leg after the set)

breathing.pattern: Breathe naturally with the rhythm of the swing.

prescription.tempo: Rhythmic, about 1.5 s per swing; let the range grow gradually
prescription.frequency: As a warm-up before running, jumping or lower-body training
prescription.progression: Larger range as the hips warm up; then without a hand support

cues.text: Stand tall on the left leg, hands on the hips (or one hand on a wall for balance), right leg relaxed.
Swing the straight right leg forward and up, then back behind you like a pendulum; the trunk stays tall and the standing knee soft.
Let the swing die down and bring the foot back beside the left.

mistakes.mistake: Leaning the trunk back on the forward swing or forward on the back swing
mistakes.fix: Stay tall; let the range come from the hip.

mistakes.mistake: Kicking hard at the end range
mistakes.fix: Smooth pendulum swings; build the range gradually.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back on the back swing
mistakes.fix: Ribs down, squeeze the glute, keep the back swing small.

kinematics.norm: Progressively higher, about 60-80 degrees once warm (clinical opinion)
About 10-20 degrees; past that the low back arches (clinical opinion)
Swinging leg nearly straight; standing knee soft (clinical opinion)
About 1.5 s per full swing (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #12544, Back Forward Leg Swings (male), video (movement reference; page not readable here)
McGill 1998, low back exercises: evidence for improving exercise regimens (Phys Ther 78(7):754-765; PMID 9672547)

cautions: Stop if you feel sharp pain in the hip, groin or back of the thigh.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
A dynamic warm-up: build the range gradually rather than kicking to the limit.
Balance problems: hold a wall or a rack upright with one hand.
modify: One hand on a wall or a sturdy support.
regressions: Standing knee raises and standing hip extensions, done slowly.

muscleNotes.hip_flexors_r: Iliopsoas and rectus femoris drive the forward swing; they are stretched at the end of the back swing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_max_r: Gluteus maximus and hamstrings drive the back swing and brake the forward swing (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.glute_med_l: Standing-side gluteus medius keeps the pelvis level on one leg (clinical opinion).
muscleNotes.core: Abdominals stop the low back arching on the back swing (clinical opinion; McGill 1998 on keeping the spine neutral).

guides.label: Right foot swings like a pendulum
